fixture: surface-gap-1.1.0 (paired against scoped-1.1.0, which omits the same module and says so)
note: Both arms ship greetlib/formatting.py, whose public render() has no api_index entry. The only difference between them is that scoped-1.1.0 declares surface_coverage: declared with formatting.py in surface_scope.exclude, and this arm declares nothing. An index silently narrower than its package claims coverage it does not have, and before 0.8.0 MIRI-PY-036 had no clause for that direction: it fired only when an entry failed to resolve, never when a definition had no entry. The first signal was a consumer failing to find a symbol that exists.

must_report_on.evidence_note: The finding must name api_index as the place the definition is missing from, not formatting.py as the place it exists. The module is not the defect; its absence from the index is.

must_not_report_on.note: Same source, same omission, declared. A linter reporting here is treating a declared scope as a defect, which would make surface_coverage unusable: the field exists so that a deliberate omission reads as a decision rather than as an incomplete index.

why_this_case_was_missing: The clause did not exist before 0.8.0, and neither did a fixture arm whose package spans more than one module. Every arm shared a single-module source, so no artifact in this repository could have exercised a rule about a surface the index fails to cover.
